Costa Rica is ideal for an itinerary where most of the time is spent in national parks and natural areas. Arenal, Poás, Irazú, Rincón de la Vieja, and Turrialba volcanoes can be paired with Monteverde's cloud forests, hot springs, and hiking routes.

On the Pacific coast, you can include Manuel Antonio, Tamarindo, the Nicoya Peninsula, and the Osa Peninsula. The Caribbean side offers a different landscape and travel style: Puerto Viejo, Puerto Limón, and Tortuguero, with its canals, rainforest, and sea turtle nesting grounds.

Corcovado, Tortuguero, and Monteverde are good places for birdwatching and wildlife encounters. Cocos Island and coastal areas can be included on a diving journey, while surfing, fishing, and motorcycle routes suit a more active program.

Ada Tours can arrange a standalone journey around Costa Rica or include the country in a combined itinerary through Central America. One trip can bring together volcanoes, jungle, hot springs, and several days by the ocean.

Cuba is well suited to a trip where urban history, music, rural regions, and beaches follow one another. In Havana, start with the old quarters, the Malecón, colonial architecture, and streets filled with vintage cars, then continue to Trinidad, Cienfuegos, Camagüey, or Santiago de Cuba.

The west adds a nature-focused stage. Pinar del Río and Viñales Valley are known for green valleys and hills, as well as areas historically linked to tobacco cultivation. This stage fits easily between Havana and a beach holiday.

For several peaceful days by the sea, choose Varadero or other island resorts. The original material also highlights Cayo Coco, Cayo Guillermo, Playa Ancón, Playa Esmeralda, and Playa del Este.

Ada Tours can create a standalone journey around Cuba or include it in a longer Caribbean and Latin American itinerary. One trip can combine cities, natural areas, and several days by the sea.

The Dominican Republic suits travelers who want to combine a beach holiday with nature and urban excursions. Punta Cana and Bávaro are known for white sand and turquoise water. La Romana and Juan Dolio on the southern coast offer calmer seas and snorkeling, while the Atlantic coast provides Puerto Plata, Sosúa, and Cabarete for surfing and kitesurfing.

Beyond the resorts, the route can continue to the Samaná Peninsula, Los Haitises National Park, and mountain areas around Jarabacoa. Los Haitises offers boat routes, mangroves, and caves, while Samaná is known for sea outings and humpback whale watching; inland areas bring waterfalls and mountain scenery.

Santo Domingo adds history: Ozama Fortress, museums, and colonial architecture offer a completely different day after beaches and nature excursions. Local cuisine and an evening of merengue can also be included.

Ada Tours can create a beach-focused itinerary or combine several regions of the Dominican Republic in one trip, with excursions, diving, snorkeling, surfing, and family days by the sea.

Ecuador straddles the equator, and its geography changes from the Pacific coast to the Andes and Amazon lowlands. Two parallel Andean ranges run through the center of the country, while the Galápagos Islands lie west of the mainland.

Quito is a convenient starting point for a journey through the highlands. From the capital, you can continue to the equator line, volcanoes, markets, and colonial cities, then add the Amazon or the Galápagos.

Climate varies considerably between regions, so choose travel dates to suit the specific itinerary. Ecuador uses the US dollar, and Spanish is the main language; Quechua and other Indigenous languages are also spoken.

El Salvador is well suited to a journey where volcanoes, lakes, national parks, and small colonial towns lie relatively close to one another. A nature itinerary can be built around Santa Ana, Los Volcanes, El Boquerón, and Coatepeque and Ilopango lakes.

The Pacific coast allows for beach days, snorkeling, and diving. The original material separately highlights Los Cóbanos Beach and its coral reef, as well as water-sport opportunities on volcanic lakes.

Continue the historical stage through Suchitoto, Santa Ana, and San Salvador. For pre-Columbian heritage, the original material mentions Joya de Cerén, San Andrés, and Tazumal.

Ada Tours can organize a journey devoted to El Salvador or combine it with Guatemala and Honduras. Hot springs, local cuisine, and several relaxed days between active nature excursions can be added.
